react_result.final_narrative_text: Five of the seven differentially abundant metabolites form a tight cluster around galactose metabolism. Galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactitol (C01697), and glycerol (C00116) all map to Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043; KEGG:hsa00052/map00052) with a fold enrichment of 1743 and an FDR of 1.22e-15 across RaMP multi-DB ORA. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently ranks KEGG:hsa00052 first with raw p = 9.533e-10, and Mummichog's empirical compound network places 'galactose metabolism' at rank 3 (p = 0.001176) using the same five driver compounds. Galactinol is the pathway-specific substrate: it is the α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol raffinose-family oligosaccharide that links galactose catabolism to inositol biochemistry. Galactitol (the alditol of galactose) and glycerol confirm the Leloir-pathway flux signature. The second cross-paradigm theme is glycerophospholipid metabolism: glycerol + myo-inositol appear in REACT:R-HSA-1483206 (FDR = 3.65e-4) and MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism (rank 4, p = 0.0051), suggesting membrane-lipid remodelling co-occurs with the carbohydrate perturbation. Acetylcholine and 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 did not reach any enriched pathway in either ORA or m/z-direct mode; they are likely background or treatment-specific hits not connected to the galactose/glycerophospholipid axis.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA and mummichog m/z-direct analysis converge on two primary pathway clusters. The dominant winner is Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00182 / KEGG:map00052), which reaches FDR = 1.22e-15 in RaMP with 5 of the 7 input metabolites detected (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) and rank 3 in mummichog (p = 4.2e-4) with all 5 confirmed. The second cross-paradigm hit is Glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR = 3.65e-4 in RaMP; MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.003 in mummichog), anchored by glycerol and myo-inositol. A third independent signal from mummichog places myo-inositol in Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (rank 2, p = 1.7e-4). Acetylcholine and 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 do not appear in any enriched pathway from either analysis, indicating they are likely peripheral or treatment-specific hits unconnected to the carbohydrate-lipid axis. The five-driver set (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) forms a coherent Leloir-pathway signature that simultaneously implicates glycerophospholipid remodelling.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA and mummichog m/z-direct analysis converge on two primary pathway clusters. The dominant winner is Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00182 / KEGG:map00052), which reaches FDR = 1.22e-15 in RaMP with 5 of the 7 input metabolites detected (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) and rank 3 in mummichog (p = 4.2e-4) with all 5 confirmed. The second cross-paradigm hit is Glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR = 3.65e-4 in RaMP; MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.003 in mummichog), anchored by glycerol and myo-inositol. A third independent signal from mummichog places myo-inositol in Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (rank 2, p = 1.7e-4). Acetylcholine and 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 do not appear in any enriched pathway from either analysis, indicating they are likely peripheral or treatment-specific hits unconnected to the carbohydrate-lipid axis. The five-driver set (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) forms a coherent Leloir-pathway signature that simultaneously implicates glycerophospholipid remodelling.
